official_sources.title: Survey Data Catalogue point density FAQ

verified_facts: 1m composite DTM covers about 99% of England
DTM removes surface objects from the DSM to model terrain surface
2022 composite uses surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022
where repeat surveys exist the newest best-resolution data is used
resampled data uses bilinear interpolation before merging
composite data is aligned to EPSG:27700
elevations are metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn with OSTN15 transformation method stated in metadata
individual surveys feeding the composite have +/-15cm RMSE vertical accuracy
metadata index catalogues identify which survey was used at a location
ground-truth points have +/-3cm RMSE and include survey date/surface/method/transformation metadata
ground-truth surveys are used to assess RMSE standard deviation and random error of timestamped LiDAR
point-cloud density is not the same as raster resolution and DTM density under vegetation may be lower than DSM density
quality_effect: Strengthens survey lineage, vertical-accuracy and density/resolution controls while preventing DSM/point-density substitution for bare-earth parcel elevation.
